title: Source: build/launcher
summary: File ownership, boundaries, state and collaborators.

Source contracts: build/launcher

build/launcher/include/platform.hpp

C++ · Tier A

Declare the compiled-image launcher platform boundary: executable/cache discovery, secure paths, build locks, installation confirmation and child supervision. POSIX and Windows implementations supply these operations for the shared launcher.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
executable_path 13 Return the platform-resolved current launcher path, or throw when it cannot be located.
cache_base 16 Choose the platform installation/cache root from supported environment/default locations; validation is a separate operation.
maintenance_directory 19 Create and return a private temporary extraction root; the launch/maintenance caller owns eventual removal.
prepare_installation_state 24 Call only after installation acceptance, before extracting the maintenance runtime. POSIX installation-only preparation of the invoking user's private HOME/.smto state directory after consent; do not invoke on ordinary read-only startup.
secure_directory 28 Create missing private cache directories and validate their ownership/ancestry according to the platform adapter.
check_directory 30 Check an existing cache directory through the platform adapter without creating or repairing it.
check_regular 32 Reject payload paths that fail the platform's regular-file/link integrity contract.
executable_mode 35 Set the extracted payload's manifest mode through the platform adapter; the caller owns path validation.
check_mode 37 Verify the platform-supported manifest permission contract without rewriting the payload.
BuildLock 40 Own a platform cache/lifecycle lease through a private implementation. Default to exclusive acquisition; callers request shared leases for concurrent compatible startup.
Impl 42 Hide the platform lock handle and release mechanism from the shared launcher interface.
BuildLock 47 Acquire the named shared/exclusive lease or throw; platform adapters define waiting and file-integrity behavior.
~BuildLock 49 Release the platform lock handle when its owning scope ends.
supervise 53 Run the selected private interpreter with the supplied argument vector and return its process status; platform adapters own signal/job-group and console handling.
confirm_installation 57 Return 0 only after a foreground terminal y/yes response, 1 on refusal, 130 on Ctrl+C. Retained interactive consent contract: only a foreground terminal y/yes response returns success; refusal returns 1 and Ctrl+C returns 130.
embedded_payload 61 Expose the Windows executable's embedded payload as an immutable pointer/length pair; its bytes remain owned by the executable resource.

build/launcher/include/sha256.hpp

C++ · Tier A

Compute SHA-256 digests inside the compiled-image launcher so extracted runtime files can be checked against the embedded manifest without importing Python. A matching digest establishes byte integrity, not publisher identity.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
Sha256 18 Maintain one incremental SHA-256 message using eight chaining words and a 64-byte block. update accepts bytes; finish mutates state to finalize once and returns lowercase hex. Use a fresh object for another message or digest.
r 26 Rotate a 32-bit word right by the nonzero sub-word counts used by the compression rounds; callers use the fixed SHA-256 rotation constants.
transform 30 Expand the current big-endian block into 64 schedule words, run the compression rounds and add their result to the chaining state. Buffer population and message-length accounting belong to update/finish.
update 60 Consume count readable bytes from data, tracking byte length and compressing each full block. The caller owns valid buffer lifetime; this method does not finalize or reset the hash.
finish 72 Append the SHA padding and 64-bit bit-length, compress the final one/two blocks and format the chaining words as 64 lowercase hex digits. Finalization is destructive and not an idempotent read.

build/launcher/src/main.cpp

C++ · Tier A

Validate and extract the embedded compiled runtime image, report startup progress and enter the selected service through the platform supervisor. File tables, digests and installation acceptance are checked before trusting the prepared runtime.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
FileEntry 29 Describe one generated manifest member: runtime/app group, relative path, contiguous compressed offset/length, expanded size, SHA-256 and allowed extraction mode. image.hpp supplies the immutable table.
StartupProgress 38 Startup diagnostics precede Python/logging initialization. Never put them on stdout, which is also used by machine-readable diagnostic and CLI commands. Own optional stderr-only startup status and a five-second still-working notifier before Python logging exists. Mutex-protected stage updates and joined shutdown keep diagnostics out of machine-readable stdout.
report 47 Write the current role, elapsed time, stage and status to stderr; callers serialize access to mutable progress state.
StartupProgress 55 Start the periodic progress thread only when visible, and wait on its condition variable so stop can wake it immediately.
step 64 Publish a new stage under the progress mutex and immediately print its starting status when progress is enabled.
stop 72 Signal the notifier and join it if still joinable. Repeated calls, including destruction after explicit stop, are safe.
~StartupProgress 78 Stop and join progress reporting on normal return or stack unwinding.
file_hash 83 Require a regular single-link file and stream it through SHA-256 in 64 KiB blocks. Throw for unreadable files or non-EOF read failure rather than returning a partial digest.
validate_table 95 Validate generated group/path identities, duplicate paths, contiguous compressed bounds, per- file expanded size up to 4 GiB and modes 0600/0700. Require the table to cover exactly the embedded payload size before extraction.
verify_tree 118 Reject unsafe tree members and unexpected files, then verify every manifest member's size/hash and optional platform mode. Owned paths receive cache checks; read-only preflight can skip derived runtime pycache directories. Unlisted empty directories are not rejected by the allowed-file set.
Payload 149 Own access to the verified application/runtime payload: macOS bundle seed trees, Windows executable resource bytes or Linux appended compressed data. Embedded checks establish integrity against compiled metadata, not independent publisher identity.
Payload 160 Verify macOS seed trees without requiring private-cache modes, or check Windows/Linux embedded size/footer and complete SHA-256 before extraction. Construction does not create the installation root.
read 189 Copy a bounded compressed payload range from Windows resource memory or the appended executable stream. The macOS extraction branch copies verified seed files instead of using this reader.
extract 202 Extract only the requested manifest group beneath prepared private directories. macOS copies verified seed files; other platforms stream DEFLATE with exact compressed/expanded limits and write checks, then apply platform modes. The provision owner verifies and publishes the whole staging tree.
provision 246 Serialize one runtime/application generation with a build lock. Verify existing immutable payloads, removing only runtime bytecode caches; otherwise require installation permission, extract/verify staging and rename it into place. Clean failed staging without overwriting an existing generation; rename is not an explicit fsync durability protocol.
bootstrap_command 282 Build isolated Python startup arguments carrying exact launcher/runtime/application identities, legal identity and approved/preflight flags into smto_bootstrap. Append the remaining caller arguments without invoking a shell; the executable bootstrap string is a protected runtime literal.
launch 303 Coordinate legal/help/version handling, read-only preflight, accepted installation/maintenance, verified extraction and lifecycle leases. Ordinary startup holds its instance lease while supervising, releases the extraction gate before Python starts, handles defined restart/maintenance exit codes and preserves deferred maintenance roots. No model execution policy is chosen here.
wmain 454 Convert Windows wide arguments to UTF-8 before the shared launch path; startup exceptions are reported on stderr with exit status 125.

build/launcher/src/posix.cpp

C++ · Tier A

Implement POSIX path ownership, file modes, cache locking and process supervision for the compiled-image launcher. These checks keep runtime extraction and child execution bound to the selected installation.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
interrupt_consent 31 Record Ctrl+C in signal-safe state so the foreground consent reader can restore its prior SIGINT handler and return cancellation.
confirm_installation 36 Retained terminal-only consent helper: require this process group to own stdin, accept a complete trimmed case-insensitive y/yes line, and return 0/1/130 for acceptance/refusal/interrupt. The current shared launch path uses the legal-consent owner instead.
executable_path 66 Locate this executable using the macOS loader plus canonicalization or Linux /proc/self/exe. Throw when discovery fails; the Linux branch returns the readlink path without a second canonicalization.
cache_base 82 Select SMTO_COMPILED_HOME first, otherwise require HOME and use macOS Application Support or Linux XDG_DATA_HOME/default local share. This chooses a path only; later directory checks enforce absolute trusted ownership.
maintenance_directory 96 Create a unique private maintenance directory under the canonical system temporary directory with mkdtemp. Return ownership to the caller, which decides when deferred maintenance permits removal.
directory_error 104 Build a cache/path diagnostic with the reason and optional observed owner/mode. This formats an error without changing ownership or permissions.
validate_ancestor 113 Require a real directory owned by the current user or root. Reject group/other-writable ancestors unless sticky; leaf privacy is checked separately.
DirectoryHandle 123 Own one directory descriptor during the no-follow HOME walk. Deleted copying prevents duplicate close; replacement and scope exit release the current descriptor.
DirectoryHandle 127 Take ownership of an already opened descriptor without opening or validating another path.
~DirectoryHandle 132 Close the owned descriptor on every scope exit, including failures during directory validation.
reset 135 Close the previous walk descriptor and take ownership of the next directory opened relative to it.
prepare_installation_state 140 After installation acceptance, securely create/repair HOME/.smto to exact mode 0700 for the installing user. Reject traversal, symlink/owner changes and swapped directory identity using descriptor-relative checks; never chown another owner. An explicit install root may omit HOME.
validate_directory 198 Walk an absolute cache path, optionally creating components, rejecting parent traversal and unsafe ancestors. Require the final directory to belong to the current user with no group/other bits; existing owner bits are not repaired. This path-based check is distinct from HOME/.smto descriptor repair.
secure_directory 217 Create missing cache directories and validate trusted ancestry plus private leaf ownership; existing unsafe directories fail instead of being repaired.
check_directory 219 Validate an existing cache path without creating it or changing its permissions.
check_regular 222 Reject symlinks, nonregular files and hard-linked payloads via lstat. Directory trust and permission verification are separate caller steps.
executable_mode 229 Apply the supplied extraction mode with chmod and throw on failure. The caller owns prior path/integrity validation; this helper does not independently fence links.
check_mode 234 Compare only the low nine permission bits with the manifest mode using lstat; type/link checks are separate and no repair occurs.
BuildLock::Impl 240 Keep the lock descriptor alive for the BuildLock lifetime; closing it releases its flock lease.
~Impl 244 Close a successfully opened lock descriptor during normal destruction or construction failure.
BuildLock::BuildLock 249 Open/create a private single-link lock file without following links, then acquire shared or exclusive flock. Retry contention/interruption every 50 ms for up to 60 seconds; unsafe ownership/type/mode or other lock errors throw.
forward_signal 268 Record shutdown and forward the received signal to the currently owned child process group. This handler does not enumerate or signal unrelated processes.
ForegroundTerminal 274 Remember terminal ownership only when this supervisor initially owns a TTY. Hand the terminal to the child group and restore the prior group at scope exit.
assign 278 Temporarily block SIGTTOU while changing stdin's foreground process group, then restore the signal mask and report whether tcsetpgrp succeeded.
ForegroundTerminal 289 Capture the current group only for foreground terminal use; noninteractive/background invocations require no terminal handoff.
handoff 294 Assign the child group when this invocation owns a terminal, or succeed without changing a terminal for other invocations.
~ForegroundTerminal 297 Attempt to restore the remembered foreground group as supervision ends; restoration failure is not thrown from the destructor.
supervise 304 Fork and exec the supplied private Python plus exact argument vector in a child process group. Gate stdin until terminal handoff, forward interrupt/termination/hangup, and escalate after a shutdown signal's 15-second grace. Reap the direct child, bound remaining group cleanup to about one second, and return its exit code or 128+signal. Linux additionally requests parent-death SIGTERM.

build/launcher/src/windows.cpp

C++ · Tier A

Implement Windows path discovery, secured runtime directories, embedded payload access and child-process supervision for the compiled-image launcher.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
interrupt_consent 19 Record Ctrl+C/Break atomically for the console consent reader and consume those control events; leave unrelated events to other handlers.
confirm_installation 26 Retained console-input consent helper: require a Windows console, read a complete line and accept trimmed case-insensitive y/yes only. Remove the temporary handler and return acceptance/refusal/interrupt status; current launch uses the legal-consent owner.
env 56 Read one Windows environment value through the wide-character API, returning an empty string when the size query has no value. This is a path-selection helper, not environment validation.
executable_path 64 Locate the current executable in a bounded wide-character buffer and reject API failure or truncation.
cache_base 72 Prefer nonempty SMTO_COMPILED_HOME, otherwise require LOCALAPPDATA and append SMTO. Later path checks own absolute-path and cache-access validation.
maintenance_directory 81 Try up to ten randomized temporary-root names and prepare the selected path through secure_directory. The caller owns cleanup; failure to find a candidate throws.
current_user 92 Copy the process token's TokenUser record and close the token handle. The returned byte vector owns the SID storage used during DACL checks.
reject_reparse 103 Reject missing paths and any reparse-point attribute. This helper does not itself prove that the object is a directory or enforce its DACL.
validate_directory 112 Require an absolute path without parent traversal, optionally create components with a protected current-user/System DACL and reject reparse points. Inspect the final DACL's ordinary allow ACEs for write grants outside user/System/Administrators; this is not the POSIX owner/mode algorithm or a complete ACL evaluator.
secure_directory 151 Create missing Windows cache components and apply the adapter's path/DACL validation; existing ACLs are inspected rather than rewritten.
check_directory 153 Run the Windows path/DACL checks without creating components or changing existing ACLs.
check_regular 156 Open a non-reparse payload for inspection, require one link and reject directory attributes, then close the handle. Parent-path validation remains with the caller.
executable_mode 166 No-op on Windows: POSIX executable mode bits do not control execution of these extracted files.
check_mode 169 No-op on Windows: payload verification uses bytes/type/link checks and Windows access controls rather than POSIX permission bits.
BuildLock::Impl 172 Own the Windows lock-file handle for the BuildLock lifetime; handle close releases the byte- range lease.
~Impl 175 Close an acquired lock-file handle during normal destruction or a failed constructor.
BuildLock::BuildLock 180 Open/create the lock file, reject a reparse path and acquire a shared/exclusive one-byte LockFileEx lease. Retry lock conflicts every 50 ms for up to 60 seconds; other errors throw. Unlike POSIX, this branch does not duplicate its lock-file owner/mode/link checks.
embedded_payload 196 Return immutable bytes and size from executable RCDATA resource 101. Reject missing resource data; the module owns its lifetime and Payload verifies its expected size/hash.
quote 205 Quote one argument for Windows process command-line parsing, doubling backslashes before quotes and at the closing quote. This builds CreateProcess input, not a cmd.exe shell command.
forward_control 218 Mark shutdown for console interrupt/break/close/shutdown and send CTRL_BREAK to the owned child group. Unrelated events remain unhandled; eventual job termination is supervised separately.
supervise 230 Create the private interpreter suspended with inherited standard handles, assign it to a kill- on-close Job Object, then resume it. Forward console stop and terminate the job after a 15-second grace. Return its exit status and close handles; explicit job breakaway is allowed, so the job is not a guarantee that every descendant or remote effect has stopped.
